one_liner: Jira is Atlassian’s issue-tracking and agile project management app. Jira Cloud is ready for agent toolkit development, with a free developer site, a public REST API, and an official MCP server.

auth.notes: Atlassian recommends OAuth 2.0 authorization code grants (3LO) for external integrations acting on a user’s behalf. Basic authentication uses an Atlassian account email and API token for simple scripts and manual calls. The bearer_token classification covers JWT authentication for legacy Connect apps, not a separate API-key scheme.

access.notes: The free path is an Atlassian Cloud developer site. Developers can authenticate with an Atlassian account and API token or register a 3LO integration in the developer console. This does not establish API entitlements on the ordinary Jira Free plan. Self-hosted Jira Data Center requires a separate installation and license; a fully functional 30-day trial is available.

api.notes: The Jira Cloud REST v3 API covers issue reads and writes, JQL search, comments, attachments, project and workflow data, and webhooks. Calls require the relevant Jira permissions.

mcp.notes: Atlassian’s hosted v2 MCP server can search Jira and create or update work items. OAuth 2.1 is the standard connection path, with optional API-token authentication. The hosted server is for Atlassian Cloud, not Data Center.

verdict.rationale: Jira Cloud offers a free, self-serve developer site and a public REST API that supports searching, creating, and updating work items. OAuth 2.0 3LO is the documented path for third-party integrations acting on a user’s behalf.
